Excellent async communication, code ownership, and ability to work with a small, senior-led team. Comfort working from a clear product brief and also proposing improvements proactively. Familiarity with logging, monitoring, and observability tools. Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process) Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare: Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n. Stack Next.js (App Router) Clerk for authentication Convex for data + backend logic n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation TypeScript Requirements Public page The fictional company name is LendLoop . Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.” Show: A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex. A “Sign in to lend or borrow” button wired to Clerk. Automation with n8n Build at least two n8n workflows: Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs. Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON. Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders.
